findings.title: Resume waits on `config !== null`, which never happens for an unpaired or cloud-only user, then fires whenever it does
findings.body: The saved page is consumed from storage at launch (`takeResumeRoute` removes the record and `decodeResumeRoute` checks its age once, `UpdateRouteKeeper.tsx:32`). The restore then waits for `config === null` to end (line 43). In `store.tsx`, `config` is `useState<ServerConfig | null>(null)` (line 392) and stays null with no paired machine selected. The store exposes a separate `configResolved` flag for exactly this case (`store.tsx:393-395`, "distinguishes 'no config yet' from 'no machine paired'"). Two consequences: (1) a user with no paired machine, or one whose host is unreachable, who restarts from a page like Settings never gets that page back; (2) the in-memory `saved` value has no age check, so if that user later pairs a machine in the same session, `config` turns non-null and the stale page is pushed over whatever they are doing. Gate on `configResolved` instead of `config === null`, so the restore runs once resolution has finished with or without a machine. If a page truly needs the machine, it should handle a missing one itself. Alternatively re-check the age when it fires.

findings.title: Failed restart is silent and `applyUpdate` can be re-entered by a quick double tap
findings.body: `applyUpdate` (`updateScreenState.ts:61`) sets the restarting phase and sleeps 900 ms before reloading, with no guard against a second call. The "Restart to update" button only becomes inert after the re-render sets `pointerEvents="none"`, so a fast double tap, or the Settings row plus the modal, can call `reloadIntoUpdate` twice, reload twice, and race the save and remove of the resume record. If the reload rejects, the screen disappears and the only trace is a `console.warn` (here and `settings/index.tsx:464`), so the user is not told the restart did not happen. A re-entry guard (return early when the phase is already `restarting`) and a visible error would cover both.

findings.title: "never reloads on its own" test cannot fail
findings.body: `reloadAsync` is created on line 33 but never passed to anything. `showUpdateReady` and `dismissUpdateScreen` take no reload API, and `ReloadApi` is only accepted by `applyUpdate` (`updateScreenState.ts:61`). The assertion on line 36 is therefore always true, whatever those functions do, so it doesn't back up the "nothing restarts without a tap" claim in the header comment of `updateScreenState.ts`. Either delete the test, or put the guarantee in a layer that can break. For example, test `shouldOfferUpdate` and `UpdatesManager` with a spy `Updates` and assert that `reloadAsync` is not called when an update is offered.

contracts.action: Tap Restart on the update screen or the Settings row: save the current page, then reload into the update
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously `Updates.reloadAsync()` was called directly from Settings and UpdatesManager (settings/index.tsx before this change); it saved nothing.
contracts.before_after: Before: the reload landed on the board. After: the page is written to AsyncStorage with a timestamp, then `reloadAsync`. A rejected reload removes the record again and rethrows.
contracts.visible_effect: The app reopens on the page the user was on, pushed over the board.
contracts.failure_mode: A `setItem` failure is swallowed and the app reopens on the board, which is acceptable. A `removeItem` failure after a failed reload leaves a record that expires after 2 minutes, so nothing else breaks.

contracts.action: Read the saved resume record at launch (unreadable-file risk)
contracts.before_after: `getItem` failure returns null and writes nothing back. `removeItem` runs only when a non-null value was read. The unreadable-then-written-back pattern does not occur: no empty default is ever persisted over the stored value.
contracts.visible_effect: Resume is skipped when storage is unreadable.
contracts.failure_mode: The user lands on the board. Nothing is lost beyond a convenience pointer.

contracts.action: Restore the saved page after launch
contracts.equivalent_path: onboarding.ts / onboardingStore.ts split, per the comment in updateResume.ts.
contracts.before_after: The record is consumed once at mount. The restore fires once, when navigation has a key and `config` is non-null. `restored` is a ref in the single root-layout instance, so it is not re-armed by remount.
contracts.visible_effect: The saved page is pushed or replaced over the board.
contracts.failure_mode: The restore never fires, or fires late with no age check, when `config` stays null (unpaired, cloud-only, or an unreachable host). See the finding.

contracts.action: Raise the update screen when an update is downloaded, and again after 15 minutes in the background
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous `onForeground` "reload" path called `Updates.reloadAsync()` silently on resume.
contracts.before_after: Now `showUpdateReady()` is shown once per update id via `lastOffered`. A resume after a long absence re-offers it. No automatic reload happens.
contracts.visible_effect: A full-screen Modal with the mascot, a Restart button and Not now.
contracts.failure_mode: Not now sets the screen back to hidden, and `lastOffered` suppresses repeats until a new update lands or a long absence passes. This is intended.

contracts.action: Test-only: exercises showUpdateReady, dismissUpdateScreen and applyUpdate against the module-level singleton state
contracts.before_after: The afterEach `reset` runs applyUpdate with a rejecting reload, which sets HIDDEN. This clears the state left in 'restarting' by the successful-reload tests (lines 39 and 49), so tests don't leak into each other.
contracts.failure_mode: Listeners from test 1 are unsubscribed, so no leakage. Test 1 relies on being the first test, because it asserts the initial hidden state.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 2.** I found one fix-level bug and one lower-confidence suggestion in this part; I did not run anything. The resume-after-restart logic in `UpdateRouteKeeper.tsx` waits on `config !== null`, which stays null for users with no paired machine or an unreachable host. Those users never get their page back, and if they pair later in the same session the stale page is pushed over whatever they are doing. The store's `configResolved` flag is the right gate. I also flagged that `applyUpdate` has no re-entry guard, so a double tap can reload twice, and that a failed reload only logs a warning with nothing shown to the user. The unreadable-store risk does not apply: `takeResumeRoute` writes nothing back when `getItem` fails. The mascot choreography, update-offer policy and tests I read look correct.

**Batch 2 of 2.** The test file is mostly sound. It covers the phase transitions, the hold-before-reload ordering, the guard against interrupting a restart, and the rethrow on reload failure. One test, \"never reloads on its own\", is vacuous: the `reloadAsync` spy is never wired to anything, so it can't fail. I'd call that a consider-level finding.
